items.title: Tommy Ridgley Interview, 1986-04-23
items.q: I think maybe, maybe McClain had left the band at that time, and Buddy Charles was playing in the band

ctx.x: We talked about who was playing guitar, and you always told me that Ernest McClain was playing, and then one time you told me Buddy Charles was playing guitar.

I think it was Buddy Charles. Jam Up, Jam Up, Jam Up, Jam Up. I was thinking it was Buddy because it's very bluesy. I think it was Buddy, because it's very bluesy. It didn't, it didn't, it didn't, it didn't, it didn't, it didn't, it didn't, it didn't, um, well, no, I don't think, I know Buddy Charles made, okay, it was Buddy Charles. Now, you know the reason why I know? Because thinking about the flip side, uh, wish I had never, that was Buddy Charles. That was Buddy Charles. That was Buddy Charles. It was not…
Well, okay, so how many, uh, so was, was Buddy like a third guitar player in the studio? I mean, McClain?
